title: Plug & Ship: Developer Anchors and Pricing Draft for Hosted API
content:
Overview
-----
This is a working brief to shape messaging and pricing microcopy for the Hosted API targeting engineers and small product teams. Goal: reduce time-to-first-success (TFS), make cost predictable, and present clear frictionless upgrade paths to paid tiers. Framing: "Plug & Ship" — mechanical sympathy for building fast without surprises.

Key developer-first value props (short, testable)
- Instant sandbox: no credit card required, sample prompts, and local mocking SDK so you can iterate off-network.
- Predictable economics: per-token meter plus simple monthly tiers for predictable throughput; visible token estimator in console and CLI.
- Production-ready defaults: sensible batching, caching suggestions surfaced in the quickstart, and model pins you can "lock" to avoid regressions.
- Fallbacks & fallthrough: automatic lower-cost variant routing when heavy load, with an opt-in policy per-API key.
- Observability from day 1: token-level breakdown and latency percentiles in console, plus an exported trace sample in the quickstart.

Quickstart angles (experiment variants)
A. "30-second Hello" (aim: reduce TFS below 60s)
- Hero line: "Start generating text in 30s — no config."
- Content: single curl + single SDK snippet + expected token cost printed as part of response example.
- CTA: "Run in console" button that injects sample prompt and shows estimated cost.
- Hypothesis: short explicit time claim increases click-to-API-key completions by 18%.

B. "Ship-mode template" (aim: mid-funnel activation)
- Ship templates: support ticket summary, email reply draft, code comment generator. Each template shows expected cost per 100 items and a recommended batching setting.
- Add a one-click deploy to demo endpoint (ephemeral API key, 24h) so product devs can test end-to-end.

C. "Local Mock → Live" (aim: reduce friction for engineering teams)
- Microcopy: "Build locally with the SDK mock; flip the switch to go live — your code doesn't change."
- Provide a 2-line env config example and a compare-and-commit checklist.

Pricing-language drafts (short-form microcopy for UI & email)
- Free tier microcopy: "Free sandbox — explore endpoints, 5k tokens/month, and local mocks. No card required."
- Pay-as-you-go: "Pay only for what you use. 0.0014 USD per generation-token (example)." (numbers TBD by finance)
- Team tier: "Team — predictable per-seat and reserved throughput for higher-volume projects. Includes role-based keys and 90-day retention exports."
- Enterprise anchor: "SLA-backed Dedicated plans, custom pricing; includes private control plane and KMS integration."
- Cost transparency line: "Estimated cost shown for every sample response — know what a single call will cost before you run it."

Pricing mechanics we should test
- Show an "estimated cost" badge on each quickstart example (A/B: badge vs no badge).
- Round-trip cost calculator in the onboarding modal (shows monthly projection for X requests/day).
- Offer an initial burst credit for first 7 days on newly-created API keys to encourage spike testing.

Competitive notes (quick scan + implications)
- OpenAI: strong brand + simple pricing but perceived black-box latency variability. Opportunity: lean into deterministic performance and per-route latency SLOs in messaging.
- Anthropic: focused safety + model guardrails — message Redwood as lower friction to run models in production with ops controls and cost levers.
- Hugging Face: community models + open ecosystem — differentiate by SLA-backed hosting and batching/quantization guidance that reduces unit cost.
- Large cloud provider endpoints: integrated infra but complex pricing — emphasize predictable unit economics and developer UX tailored for product teams.
Implication: messaging should call out "predictable cost" and "production SLOs" as primary differentiators for teams beyond experiment stage.

Sample hero copy candidates (for landing page/hero card)
- Option 1: "Ship LLM features — fast, predictable, and under control."
- Option 2: "From first request to scale — one API, consistent performance."
- Option 3: "Build fast, ship safely — hosted inference with cost clarity."

Microcopy for pricing modal (dialog)
- Header: "Estimate your monthly bill"
- Line 1: "Enter expected requests per day and median tokens per request."
- Outcome: "Estimated monthly spend: $X — includes recommended batching to save up to Y%."

Conversion experiments (A/B candidates with success metrics)
- Experiment 1: Estimated-cost badge on quickstart example → track API key creation rate, sign-ups that hit first 1k tokens.
- Experiment 2: "Ephemeral demo endpoint" vs "No ephemeral demo" → measure conversion to paid trial and time-to-first-customer-request.
- Experiment 3: CTA wording test: "Start for free" vs "Try without a card" → sign-up completions.
- Experiment 4: Pricing page showing both PAYG per-token and monthly committed discounts (accordion) vs single condensed view → measure contact-sales clicks for high-volume usage.

Operational notes for docs/engineering handoff
- Embeddable cost badge component (web): props: estimatedTokens, currency, tooltip with method. Prioritize small footprint and server-side renderable.
- Quickstart repo: add scripts that print estimated token usage of example prompts at build time. Link in console onboarding.
- SDKs: ensure mock mode toggles via REDWOOD_MOCK=true and returns token-count metadata on responses.

Open questions / things to resolve
- Finance needs the baseline per-token numbers and the committed discount ladders to finalize public copy. (JIRA-GT-341 assigned)
- Legal: what language is required for the "ephemeral demo endpoints" and retention? (Ping security/compliance)
- Product: which three templates ship in the initial quickstart? Need prioritization.
- Engineering: how long to build an ephemeral demo endpoint and the cost-metering badge? Rough estimate requested.

Next steps (owner + timeline)
- Maya: finalize 2 hero copy lines and run 3 small landing experiments (2 weeks).
- Jared: prototype cost-badge component and hook into quickstart repo (1 sprint).
- Sofia: coordinate legal & privacy review for ephemeral demos (blocker for demo rollout).
- Evan: run initial A/B for estimated-cost badge on internal beta (2 weeks).

Appendix: example quickstart snippets (for copy use)
1) curl quickstart (30s)
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \n  -d '{"model": "redwood-alpha-1", "prompt": "Summarize this email in one sentence."}'

Response (example):
{"summary":"Can you join the meeting at 3pm?", "_estimated_tokens": 42, "_estimated_cost_usd": "0.03"}

2) Node SDK (mock → live)
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, mock: process.env.REDWOOD_MOCK === 'true' });
const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-alpha-1', prompt: 'Draft a reply to a bug report.' });
console.log(res.output, res._meta.cost);

Notes to self: keep copy punchy, minimize corporate nouns. This doc should seed landing, console, quickstart repo README, and the pricing modal.

Unresolved edits: please add any quick CTA microcopy variants you want tested.
